title: Odia Cinema: A Living Screen
subtitle: Stories, People and Places Between
scope: Editorial book plan only. Read all eleven current chapter bodies, manifest, retained placement audit and documentary provenance. No canonical edits, new acquisition or historical research. No fresh visual/PDF render audit.
arc: Use the parent’s refined three-part order. The overview and AIR establish overlapping creative worlds; the central chapters follow production, performance, households, livelihoods and representation through particular people and films; television and OTT close with changing conditions of making and encountering stories. The arrangement is thematic, not a claim that one medium supersedes another.
preface:
A film can begin in a familiar household and lead us towards questions we had not thought to ask. Who makes the decisions? Whose work remains outside the frame? How does a story find its viewers, and what allows it to survive for generations?

This book follows those questions through selected films, careers and institutions connected with Odisha. Its chapters move between literature and performance, artistic choices and working lives, recognition and access. They invite readers to notice a composer beside a director, a production team beside a performer, and the people represented by a story beside the person telling it.

The selection is an invitation to explore further. Published credits, archives, interviews and criticism provide its foundations; where their evidence differs or remains incomplete, the distinction matters. A remembered success, a festival selection and a recorded award each tell a different story.

Read these chapters in sequence or follow a curiosity. Return to the works, compare accounts, and look for the names that deserve another conversation. A living screen leaves room for the next viewer to ask something new.
